title: Crème Brûlée for Two
short: Silky vanilla custard under a glassy, crackling sugar crust.
keywords: Crème Brûlée for Two, date night, dinner for two, fancy, classic
intro: Crème brûlée is the definition of a restaurant dessert, but it's mostly waiting. The custard bakes gently in a water bath and chills for hours; the dramatic part, torching the sugar until it turns to amber glass, happens at the table.
why: Tapping through the burnt-sugar crust is a little celebration, and torching it in front of your guest is unforgettable.

video.title: How to make a crème brûlée

ings.h: 240 ml (1 cup)

ings.i: vanilla bean, split (or 1 tsp vanilla extract)

ings.h: 40 g (3 tbsp)
ings.i: sugar, plus 2 tbsp for the topping

steps.t: Heat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Warm the cream with the vanilla seeds and pod until steaming, then take it off the heat and steep for 10 minutes.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt just until combined; you want to avoid bubbles.
Slowly whisk the warm cream into the yolks. Strain into a jug and skim off any foam.
Pour into two shallow 150–180 ml ramekins set in a baking dish. Add hot water to halfway up their sides.
Bake 30–40 minutes until the edges are set and the center jiggles like jelly (77–79°C / 170–175°F).
Remove from the water, cool for 30 minutes and chill for at least 3 hours or up to 2 days.
To serve, blot the surface dry, sprinkle each with 1 tbsp sugar, tip off the excess and torch in small circles until deep amber. Rest 1–2 minutes so the crust hardens.

tips: No torch? Broil on the top rack for 1–3 minutes, watching every second.
Shallow, wide ramekins give more crust per spoonful.
makeahead: Bake up to 2 days ahead. Torch just before serving.
plating: Place the ramekin on a small plate with a doily or napkin and two berries.

faq.a: It needed longer in the oven. Check the wobble: set edges, jiggly middle.
